qa.reply:
Yes
From the QA lens, this directly ensures every rule and variation is tested red first. Requiring the corpus to hold input encodings upfront and committing neighbour variants before each fix round's red step guarantees that unhandled encodings and regression-prone neighbour shapes fail red before implementation. This prevents escapes and ensures test checks catch the specific violations they name without passing bad state.
